articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These designations aim to disrupt the financial networks of those who support illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally.
Further details on the specific individuals and entities targeted, as well as the implications of these designations, are available on the Treasury website.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designation List
body: OFAC issued an update to its Iran designation list on November 9, 2026.
This action reflects the ongoing U.S. efforts to address Iran's destabilizing activities and its support for terrorism.
The updated list includes modifications to existing entries, and parties are advised to review the changes for compliance purposes.

articles.headline: New Iran-Related Designations Announced by OFAC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.
These designations are part of the U.S. government's comprehensive strategy to counter the Iranian regime's malign influence and its nuclear proliferation activities.
The action targets specific individuals and entities contributing to Iran's illicit activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-Related and Transnational Criminal Organizations; Issues Cuba Designations and Determination
body: OFAC announced new designations on November 5, 2026, targeting cyber-related threats and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new designations related to Cuba.
The action against cyber actors and criminal organizations aims to disrupt their financial operations and protect the U.S. financial system from illicit activities.
Additionally, a Cuba-related determination was published, further clarifying U.S. policy towards the island nation.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Updates Listings, Publishes Alert, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: On November 4, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations and provided updates to certain existing Iran-related listings.
The agency also published an Iran-related OFAC Alert to inform the public about potential risks and compliance obligations.
Furthermore, an amended Venezuela-related General License and a new Frequently Asked Question were issued, providing guidance on authorized transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment provides updated guidance and authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran, aiming to clarify the scope of permissible activities.
Parties engaging in Iran-related transactions should review the amended General License to ensure ongoing compliance.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities in North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: OFAC announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities in North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities, including proliferation financing from North Korea and human rights abuses and corruption in the DRC.
The designations underscore the U.S. commitment to promoting stability and accountability in these regions.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: On October 26, 2026, OFAC issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments provide updated guidance and clarifications for financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under OFAC regulations.
The updated FAQs are crucial for ensuring proper compliance procedures and accurate reporting of sanctions-related activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related, Russia-Related General Licenses; Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses on October 21, 2026, providing authorizations for certain transactions.
Concurrently, OFAC removed several designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a shift in sanctions policy for specific entities.
Additionally, amended Frequently Asked Questions were issued to provide further clarity on these changes and their implications.

articles.headline: OCC Announces October 2026 Enforcement Actions Against Banks and IAPs
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026, targeting deficiencies in Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance programs and other violations.

Actions against banks include a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million Civil Money Penalty against American Express National Bank for BSA compliance program deficiencies, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and customer due diligence violations.

Additionally, a $750 million Civil Money Penalty was assessed against Bank of America, National Association, for similar BSA compliance program failures, including issues with suspicious activity reporting and inaccurate transmittor name information in wire transfers.

articles.headline: BIS Extends Suspension of 'Affiliates Rule' Until January 10, 2027
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has extended the suspension of its interim final rule, known as the 'Affiliates Rule,' until January 10, 2027.

This rule, originally set to take effect on November 10, 2026, expands export control restrictions under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to companies owned or controlled by parties on certain restricted party lists.

The extension provides additional time for businesses with international operations, particularly those with connections to China, to review and update their screening procedures and trade compliance programs.

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.
This deregulatory action aims to align export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms, reducing compliance burdens on the firearms industry while maintaining national security.

Under this new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), requiring a license for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, with license exceptions similar to those available for firearms.

articles.headline: WuXi AppTec Removed from Chinese Military List, Risk of Relisting Remains
body: The U.S. Deputy Secretary of Defense has decided to delist WuXi AppTec from the department's 1260H list under the U.S. National Defense Authorization Act, as published in the Federal Register on November 9, 2026.
This removal follows WuXi AppTec's preliminary injunction in August, which temporarily blocked the U.S. government from enforcing its designation.

However, the notice explicitly states that the removal is 'without prejudice to relisting the company on additional or supplementary grounds,' indicating a continued risk of redesignation as the company's court case with the Department of Defense is ongoing.

articles.headline: Extension of the Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities

The suspension was set to end November 9, 2026. This final rule extends the suspension through January 10, 2027.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
